summary: Source-anchored research for Lighter zero-fee perpetuals and API. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Fee-free status is a per-market setting that Lighter has changed before. All RWA perp markets traded with 0 fees across every fee and staking tier in March 2026, and in April 2026 RWA market fees turned back on, applied based on tier. In April 2026 Lighter added is_taker_fee_enabled and is_maker_fee_enabled fields to the orderBookDetails endpoint so clients can verify markets where fees are disabled, and said only $LIT had maker fees set to zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-18)

A Lighter API key is a keypair separate from the Ethereum key. Each key is bound to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and has its own nonce stream. Usable key indexes are 4 to 254. Indexes 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's apps (on Robinhood Chain, 157 is also reserved), and 255 is only for querying all keys. Registering a key uses ChangePubKey, which always needs an L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

In a November 2026 announcement Lighter said new per-IP WebSocket limits take effect on Lighter Core after the scheduled downtime on Sunday, November 22. Standard / public, Plus and base Premium get 50 connections, 1,000 subscriptions, 200 unique accounts and 200 client messages per 60 seconds. Premium 1 and above get 255 connections, 5,000 subscriptions, 5,000 unique accounts and 1,000 client messages per 60 seconds; Builder gets 255, 10,000, 10,000 and 10,000. Only connections authenticated with the Authorization handshake header receive tier limits, while Plus and base Premium retain Standard limits even when authenticated. The rate-limits docs page still listed the older limits of 255 connections and 5000 subscriptions per IP. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On the morning of November 16 (UTC) an attacker recovered API private keys from public signatures because the affected accounts used unsafe signing code other than the official Lighter SDKs that reused signing nonces, then moved funds through a public pool: create a public pool from the affected account, mint pool shares in a separate attacker-controlled account, transfer the affected account's funds into the pool (increasing NAV without minting pool shares), redeem the shares and withdraw. Lighter says its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. Bitquery traced one withdrawal of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC to a single wallet that swapped it to ETH in four minutes and sent 1,920 ETH through twelve new wallets to Hyperliquid, where each one bought XMR1. (high confidence)

lighter-go v1.0.13 retracts v1.0.1 because GenerateAPIKey with a non-empty seed produced weak, predictable API keys, and tells users to upgrade and rotate any API key generated with a seed. The same release bumps golang.org/x/crypto for a critical vulnerability and requires Go 1.26. (low confidence)

Third-party connectors have had real-money defects on Lighter. Hummingbot issue 8504 (state: open) reports Lighter perp market orders that Lighter executed successfully but that Hummingbot recorded as FILLED with executed_amount_base = 0 and no trade fills. The issue notes that trade-history polling queries the market-wide /api/v1/recentTrades endpoint, whose sample BTC-USDC response covered only ~9.5 seconds of market trades, so it can miss the account's fills; whether that happened for these two orders was not established. Hummingbot issue 8309 (now closed) reported repeated 429 Too Many Requests errors on Lighter when perpetual APIs were enabled. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bubblemaps and Bitquery both report a withdrawal of about $10.39M from Lighter on 16 November 2026. Bubblemaps says the attacker deposited $20k into Lighter and withdrew $10.39M about 36 minutes later. Bitquery traced one transfer of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC, swapped $10.36 million of it to ETH on CoW Swap, and sent ETH to Hyperliquid, where each wallet bought XMR1. Posts on X put the loss at $15.5 million across two market maker accounts; Bitquery says a second amount, reported at $5.09 million, had not left Lighter when it last read the chain. (high confidence)

An API response with code 200 means the transaction was accepted, not executed. When the outcome is unknown (timeout, dropped connection, no WebSocket confirmation), do not re-sign blindly. Check the transaction status by hash or the account_tx channel, and compare nextNonce with the nonce used. Re-signing with a new nonce while the original may still execute can place the order twice. Reusing the same clientOrderIndex rejects a duplicate only while the first order is still open. (high confidence)

Lighter's troubleshooting page maps symptoms to causes. invalid nonce (21104): two processes use one API key concurrently, or an earlier transaction failed in the sequencer without consuming its nonce; batch nonces must be consecutive (21105). invalid PublicKey, please run changePubKey (21108): the key is not registered at that index, or another app replaced it at the same index. Signature rejected: the chainId must be 304 for mainnet and 300 for testnet. HTTP 429 or 405: rate limited, so back off, authenticate requests, reduce polling (use WebSocket) or change tier. account not found (21100) after a deposit: deposits take a few minutes to credit (CCTP: ~15–20 min). WebSocket disconnects come from no frame within 2 minutes, too many subscriptions, reading too slowly, or a server deployment. (high confidence)

Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can buy volume quota with USDC on Lighter mainnet through POST /api/v1/buyVolumeQuota at 0.0005 USDC per quota (1,000,000 quota = 500 USDC). A single request can buy at most 15,000,000 quota, and the balance after the purchase must not exceed 30,000,000; trading alone refills the balance only up to 15,000,000. The payment is an L2Transfer that you sign and pass as tx_info. lighter-python users should use client.sign_transfer() to obtain the signed tx_info and not client.transfer(), because it submits the transfer through sendTx, moving the payment asset without purchasing quota. The endpoint is not available on testnet. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On Lighter, Standard accounts (the default) pay 0 maker and 0 taker fees on regular perpetual and spot orders. They pay 1 bp (0.01%) on TWAP/advanced orders and RFQ. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts are subject to maker and taker fees. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Standard accounts pay for zero fees in latency: taker orders, cancels and modifies wait 300ms, while maker orders have 0ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have 140 ms taker latency, and their cancels and post-only placements carry no added latency. Premium fees start at 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker, falling by up to 30% (0.0028% / 0.0196%) with 500,000 staked LIT. LIT stake is aggregated per L1 address across sub-accounts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On a Standard account maker latency is 0ms, while cancel/modify latency is 300ms. Premium/Advanced accounts have no additional latency on cancels and post-only placement. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter had a serious outage during the October 11, 2025 market-wide liquidation event. Phemex reports three transaction batches were lost and the liquidity pool (LLP) fell 5.35%. Beosin identified dependence on a single sequencer and ZK-SNARK proof generation bottlenecks as key factors, and the CEO admitted a delayed database upgrade hindered the platform. Separately, On Chain Times says that on October 10th LLP took a 5% loss and LLP holders were compensated in points. (medium confidence)

Critics argue the zero fee is not free. An HTX-hosted analysis puts the standard account's actual cost at 6-12 basis points per trade, 5-10 times higher than the premium account's 0.2-2 basis points per trade, using typical volatility levels (50–80% annualized) and an informed-trader advantage of 2–5 times. TrueHold gives a comparison: a $10,000 position opened and closed with market orders costs $0 on a Lighter standard account and $5.60 on Premium before discounts, but 300 ms of slippage can cost more than a 0.028% taker fee for traders who take liquidity often in fast markets. (low confidence)

Premium/Advanced is the opt-in tier suitable for HFT, the lowest latency on Lighter. On Lighter mainnet it charges 0.0040% maker and 0.0280% taker before discounts, gives a 140ms taker delay for all tiers, and adds no latency to cancels or post-only placements. Staking LIT cuts fees by 2.5% at 1,000 LIT up to 30% at 500,000 LIT (0.0028% maker, 0.0196% taker). Stake is summed per L1 address across sub-accounts, and fee credits count as staked LIT. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Standard accounts have 300ms taker latency, 300ms cancel latency and 0ms post-only latency. Premium removes the delay on cancels and post-only placement and sets the taker delay at 140ms. A batch waits for the longest speed bump of any transaction in it, so mixing a taker order into a batch of post-only orders delays all of them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

API trading uses transactions signed with SignerClient and sent with the sendTx or sendTxBatch REST endpoints, or the jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch WebSocket types. A batch holds up to 50 transactions from the same account and API key with consecutive nonces. REST batches of up to ~15 orders are safe because request-body size limits at the CDN edge can reject a large REST batch; WebSocket messages are limited to 64 KB. A response of code: 200 only means the transaction was accepted, so subscribe to account_orders/{market}/{account} or account_tx/{account} to see fills and rejections. (high confidence)

Lighter's own tier guidance: Standard is suitable for retail and latency-insensitive traders; Plus is suitable for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits and keeps the 300 ms taker latency; Premium/Advanced is suitable for HFT, with 140 ms taker latency and no additional latency on cancels or post-only placement. On Standard, the zero maker delay applies to post-only orders, and Standard accounts share 60 requests/minute across reads and transactions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

The zero fee is a growth subsidy, so treat the fee schedule as changeable. A Medium fundamentals review says Lighter chose growth before monetization (Standard users pay nothing, Premium users pay for faster execution) and reports gross protocol revenue of Q4 2025: $39.7M, Q1 2026: $19.7M, Q2 2026: $9.6M and Q3 2026 so far: ~$4.7M. ForkLog reported on 19.01.2026, citing CryptoRank analysts, that weekly volume has decreased nearly 3x from its peak as the airdrop is distributed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-22)

Common Lighter API errors and fixes: invalid nonce (21104) means two processes use one API key concurrently or an earlier transaction failed in the sequencer without consuming its nonce, so refetch nextNonce and re-sign; batch nonces must be consecutive (21105); invalid PublicKey, please run changePubKey (21108) means the key is not registered or was replaced by another app using the same index; the chainId must be 304 for mainnet and 300 for testnet; HTTP 429 or 405 means rate limited; WebSocket drops come from no frame within 2 minutes (send pings every ~60 s and reconnect automatically); account not found (21100) after a deposit usually means deposits take a few minutes to credit (CCTP: ~15–20 min). (medium confidence)

A Binance Square article (Nov 18, 2025) put Lighter's trading volume/OI ratio at 8.03 in one place and 8.19 in another, against 1.57 for Hyperliquid, and read it as points-based exploitation or points-driven trading. Castle Labs, using DefiLlama data for 17 August to 15 September 2026, put Lighter's turnover at 2.87x a day against 1.16x for Hyperliquid, and said Jupiter Perps, Pacifica and GMTrade trade 7x to 9x their open interest daily. Castle's top perp DEXs by open interest table dated 22 November 2026 lists Lighter at $538.9M open interest, 5.6% share and -29% 30-day change. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter's own post-mortem post says that during the 4.5 hour period from 10:30PM EST on October 10, 2025 until 3AM EST on October 11, 2025, Lighter experienced its first serious outage since mainnet private beta in January and public launch on October 1. Phemex reports that the outage lost three transaction batches and cut the LLP liquidity pool by 5.35%, that Beosin blamed the single sequencer and ZK-SNARK proof-generation bottlenecks, and that the CEO admitted a delayed database upgrade hindered the platform. (medium confidence)

Plus accounts are the opt-in tier for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits. They pay 0.005% maker and taker, keep 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and 0ms maker latency, and get 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute, 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute and 16 sub-accounts. Standard accounts can create up to 4 sub-accounts, which cannot be deleted. The tier is switched with the `changeAccountTier` endpoint; downgrades require a 24-hour cooldown after the last tier change. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter mainnet and Lighter on Robinhood Chain have separate base URLs and rate-limit tables. Lighter mainnet uses https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai; Lighter on Robinhood Chain uses https://api.rh.lighter.xyz (chain ID 466324), with Builder 150,000, Plus 120,000 and Premium 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On Lighter mainnet, Standard accounts (the default) pay 0 maker and 0 taker on regular perpetual and spot orders. Since an August 2026 change they pay 0.01% (1 bp) on TWAP, Chase Limit and RFQ orders. Plus and Premium accounts continue to pay their normal tier fees. Limit and market orders remain free for Standard accounts, and binary options have a separate fee model. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On Lighter mainnet the Plus tier is the opt-in tier for latency-insensitive users looking for increased rate limits. It charges 0.005% maker and taker, keeps the 300 ms taker and cancel/modify latency and 0ms maker latency, and allows 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute, 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute and 16 sub-accounts. Standard allows 4 sub-accounts and Premium 64, and sub-accounts cannot be deleted. Plus is enabled with the `changeAccountTier` endpoint or in the app. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

REST limits depend on tier. Standard accounts get 60 requests per rolling minute, unweighted, with no separate sendTx bucket. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and read-only endpoints fall into a separate bucket from sendTx and sendTxBatch. Builder accounts, free of charge on application through Discord, get 240,000 weighted requests per rolling minute. Limits apply to both IP address and L1 address, and authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405, and a firewall block lasts 60 seconds. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On a Standard account every call competes for the same 60 requests per minute, including nonce and reconciliation reads, and weight-3,000 endpoints permit only eight calls/minute. Opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) also counts against the REST limit, and once it is exhausted new WebSocket connections receive HTTP 429. NautilusTrader suggests 15 transaction requests and 5 REST calls/minute for bounded Standard testing, and a Hummingbot issue opened on Jun 18, 2026 reports repeated 429 Too Many Requests errors on the Lighter perpetual private websocket connection and candle polling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

API keys belong to one account index (master, sub-account or pool) and each has its own key pair and nonce. Indexes 0–254 exist, 0–3 are reserved for Lighter's web/mobile apps, and 255 is a special index only for querying apikeys. Registering a key requires the L1 wallet signature (or an on-chain call). A key can trade, cancel, modify, change leverage and margin, create sub-accounts, make secure withdrawals (which can only go back to the L1 address that created the account) and make same-owner transfers. It cannot alone transfer to another L1 owner, fast-withdraw or approve an integrator with fees. Auth tokens last at most 8 hours, and Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Premium/Advanced accounts can mark up to 251 API keys per account index as maker-only. These keys are restricted to 0ms speed bump transactions only (post-only (ALO) orders, modifies of ALO orders, cancel and cancel all) and get an optimized execution path with reduced scheduling latency. Order types with a speed bump sent via a maker-only key are rejected with error 62007, a 1-hour cooldown applies between api key type changes (error 62008), and Standard accounts are rejected (error 62009). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Each API key has its own transaction nonce, by default previous plus one, and the SkipNonce attribute allows jumps that stay below `2^47 - 1`. When a transaction fails without consuming its nonce, any transactions already sent on the same key with higher nonces fail too and must be re-signed starting from the current `nextNonce`. Failures while the sequencer applies the transaction (invalid size or price, duplicate `clientOrderIndex`, wrong reduce-only direction) do consume the nonce. An `invalid nonce` (21104) error can come from two processes using the same API key concurrently, so use one key per process, or serialize. (high confidence)

Order parameters: price is an integer scaled by 10^price_decimals and, for taker orders, is the worst acceptable price (the order is cancelled if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price); timeInForce is 0 Immediate-or-cancel, 1 Good-till-time or 2 Post-only; orderExpiry is a Unix ms timestamp between 5 minutes and 30 days ahead, with 0 for IOC orders; clientOrderIndex is a uint48 unique across all markets. The minimum order is the larger of min_base_amount and min_quote_amount. (medium confidence)

Third-party frameworks support Lighter. NautilusTrader's nautilus-lighter crate provides Rust data and execution clients, and its Python extension exposes configuration, deployment and environment selection, factories, and integrator revocation. Hummingbot has a spot connector and a perpetual connector (ID lighter_perpetual, supports testnet) with order types LIMIT, LIMIT_MAKER and MARKET. Lighter's own packages include lighter-sdk on PyPI (latest version 1.1.9), lighter-go v1.0.13 (Go 1.26 is now required) and the Lighter Agent Kit, a skill that lets AI agents trade on Lighter. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

A leaked key that can trade can still lose money. Lighter's postmortem says someone holding your key could place orders from your account that trade against their own orders at bad prices, which works best in thinly traded markets, or open large or highly leveraged positions, even though an API key can't withdraw funds to anyone else's wallet. Lighter announced IP whitelists for API keys, configurable permissions and limits per API key, and monitoring for nonce reuse. A Cointelegraph article published Nov 17, 2026 said Lighter plans IP allowlists and configurable permissions for individual keys. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter's first serious outage ran 4.5 hours, from 10:30PM EST on October 10, 2025 until 3AM EST on October 11, 2025, since mainnet private beta in January and public launch on October 1. LLP holders experienced an asset decline of about 5% in the same event. Sources differ on cause: Foresight News (via Binance Square) said the disruption was attributed to the team's failure to upgrade infrastructure in a timely manner, ChainCatcher (via Bitget) relayed a database failure, and Beosin blamed the single sequencer and ZK-SNARK proof-generation bottlenecks. Lighter announced 250,000 points of compensation, and preliminary data showed 38 traders faced losses surpassing $100,000. (medium confidence)

Lighter states that an API key can't withdraw funds to anyone else's wallet, because withdrawals only ever go to the account owner's own wallet. It also states that a key that can trade can still lose money for its owner if someone else holds it. Besides the pool route, Lighter names two risks. Someone holding the key could place orders from the account that trade against their own orders at bad prices, which works best in thinly traded markets. They could also open large or highly leveraged positions that expose the account to heavy losses or liquidation. (high confidence)

Lighter's docs list what an API key can do alone: trade, cancel, modify, leverage/margin, sub-accounts, secure withdrawals, same-owner transfers, and auth-gated REST and WebSocket reads. Secure withdrawals only need the API key because they can only go back to the L1 address that created the account. Alone it cannot make transfers to another L1 owner, fast withdrawals or approve an integrator with fees; a Transfer needs an L1 signature when sender and receiver have different owners, and ApproveIntegrator needs one when the integrator has a different owner and at least one max fee is > 0. Transfers between the same owner's accounts need no L1 signature. After the November 16 incident, Lighter also requires a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Premium/Advanced accounts can mark up to 251 API keys per account index as maker-only. These keys are restricted to 0ms speed bump transactions only (post-only (ALO) orders, modifies of ALO orders, cancel and cancel all) and have an optimized execution path that skips the speed-bump queue. Keys reserved by the front-end (0-3) cannot be set as maker-only, and a one-hour cooldown applies between changes. The setMakerOnlyApiKeys and getMakerOnlyApiKeys endpoints set and list maker-only keys. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter queues transactions per API key, and each transaction waits for a speed bump before it executes (for example, on Standard, taker orders wait 300 ms and post-only orders 0 ms). A slow transaction delays everything sent after it on the same key: a post-only order sent right after a taker order on the same key waits for the taker order's 300 ms. A batch waits for the longest speed bump of any transaction in it, so mixing a taker order into a batch of post-only orders delays all of them. Lighter's guidance is a dedicated key per workload, for example one for quoting/cancelling, one for taking, one for transfers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Each Lighter API key has its own transaction nonce, by default new_nonce = previous_nonce + 1. The SkipNonce attribute allows a jump if the new nonce exceeds the previous one; a skip-nonce jump must stay below 2^47 - 1 and the absolute nonce cap is 2^48 - 1. A rejection by the API server (bad signature, wrong nonce, rate limit, ExpiredAt less than ~5 s away, not enough margin for a resting order) does not consume the nonce, and neither does a sequencer rejection before the transaction is applied. Rejections while the sequencer applies the transaction (invalid size or price, duplicate clientOrderIndex, wrong reduce-only direction, cancelling or modifying an unknown order) do consume it. When a transaction fails without consuming its nonce, the higher-nonce transactions already sent on that key fail too, so re-sign from the current nextNonce. (high confidence)

Order and batch field rules, from Lighter's signing guide: orderExpiry is a Unix ms timestamp between 5 minutes and 30 days ahead, and 0 for IOC orders. clientOrderIndex is a uint48 (at most 2^48−1) that is unique across all markets. For taker orders, price is the worst acceptable price: if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price, the order is cancelled. A batch holds up to 50 transactions from the same account and API key with consecutive nonces. REST batches of up to ~15 orders are safe because request-body size limits at the CDN edge can reject a large REST batch; WebSocket jsonapi/sendtxbatch accepts messages up to 64 KB, enough for 50 orders. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

WebSocket rules from Lighter's docs: clients must send at least one frame every 2 minutes (a WebSocket ping frame or any application-level message; {"type":"ping"} returns {"type":"pong"}). Writes to slow clients time out after 250 ms by default, so reconnect and resubscribe for fresh snapshots. Subscribe requests use slash-separated channel names while response channel values use colons. The order book channel sends new orders in batches every 50ms and a complete snapshot on subscription; a client can verify continuity by checking that begin_nonce on the current update matches the nonce of the previous update. Private channels take an auth token inside the subscribe message, while public-pool data does not require authentication. jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch send transactions over the websocket. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

On Standard accounts the limit of 60 requests per rolling minute is unweighted and covers transactions too: Standard accounts have no separate sendTx bucket and are still bound to the 60 requests per minute limit. The Transaction Type Limits table (default 40 requests per minute; L2Withdraw 2 per minute and 3 per 2 hours) applies to all account types. For Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts, each sendTx or sendTxBatch request costs 6 weight from a separate bucket, a batch counts as one request, and no IP limits are enforced, only L1 address limits. Builder accounts raise only the read-only limits; otherwise standard account limits apply. Opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) counts against the REST rate limit, and when that limit is exhausted new WebSocket connections receive HTTP 429. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hummingbot issue 8309 (opened on Jun 18, 2026) reports repeated 429 errors when Lighter perpetual APIs were enabled. The websocket handshake to wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream failed with WSServerHandshakeError 429, and GET https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/api/v1/candles returned HTTP status 429 with {"code":23000,"message":"Too Many Requests!"}. After removing the perpetual APIs and retrying with spot only, the problem was no longer reproducible. Lighter's docs say opening a WebSocket (GET /stream, weight 90) counts against the REST rate limit. (medium confidence)

Lighter and Lighter on Robinhood Chain expose the same REST API, WebSocket API and transaction format, but are separate exchanges: accounts, balances, API keys, nonces and account indexes don't carry over, and mainnet signatures use distinct chain IDs. Lighter mainnet is https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai (chain ID 304), Lighter testnet is https://api.testnet.lighter.xyz (300), Lighter on Robinhood Chain mainnet is https://api.rh.lighter.xyz (466324) and Lighter on Robinhood Chain testnet is https://api.rh-testnet.lighter.xyz (300). Lighter's agent rules say to default to testnet in examples and tests. Rate-limit tables are listed separately for each deployment. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Standard accounts face a 60 requests per rolling minute REST limit, unweighted. Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts get 24,000 weighted requests per rolling minute and Builder accounts (free, applied for via Discord) get 240,000. Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 or 405. A firewall block lasts 60 seconds; an API-server cooldown follows `weightOfEndpoint/(totalWeight/60)`. Opening a WebSocket (weight 90) counts against the REST limit. Authenticating each request means only L1-based limits apply instead of IP-based limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter mainnet and Lighter on Robinhood Chain have separate base URLs and rate-limit tables. Lighter mainnet uses https://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai and signing chain ID 304, Lighter on Robinhood Chain uses https://api.rh.lighter.xyz and chain ID 466324, and testnets use 300. In the Robinhood Chain tables, Standard has 200 ms maker/cancel latency and 8 sub-accounts, Plus pays 0.015% with 8000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 120000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium fees and limits follow last 14D volume (0.0120% maker, 0.0350% taker below $1M) instead of staked LIT. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

In October 2025 Lighter said a runaway bot jammed through the HYPE book with size, that there were no liquidations or other adverse effects, and that the wick was scrubbed from the front end. CoinDesk reported that HYPE briefly surged to $98 on Lighter at a steep premium compared to global prices, that all on-chain transaction data remains transparent and accessible on blockchain explorers, and that crypto analyst Duo Nine criticized the removal of the data as masking deeper liquidity issues. (medium confidence)

The 'zero fee is a latency tax' critique is a model, not a measurement. A MarsBit article (last updated on 2025-12-11) puts the standard account's actual cost at 6-12 basis points per trade versus 0.2-2 basis points on the premium account (5-10 times higher), using typical volatility levels (50–80% annualized) and an informed-trader advantage of 2–5 times. Leviathan News repeated the 5–10× claim on its X account. TrueHold frames the trade-off as a choice: a $10,000 position opened and closed with market orders costs $0 on a Lighter standard account and $5.60 on Premium before discounts, and 300 ms of slippage can cost more than a 0.028% taker fee for traders who take liquidity often in fast markets. (medium confidence)

Lighter auth tokens are signed with an API key and each can have a maximum expiry of 8 hours, with the structure {expiry_unix}:{account_index}:{api_key_index}:{random_hex}. REST sends the token as the Authorization header; WebSocket sends it as "auth" inside the subscribe message. Authenticating a request makes it count against the L1 address instead of the IP. Read-only tokens (structure ro:{account_index}:{single|all}:{expiry_unix}:{random_hex}) cannot sign transactions, have a maximum expiry of 10 years and a minimum of 5 minutes, and cover one account index (single) or the master account and its sub-accounts (all). On Lighter, tokens/create costs 10,000 request weight, so create tokens once and store them. Lighter says to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Hard-coded numbers in third-party connectors can disagree with Lighter's docs. Hummingbot's Lighter connector constants say the table matches the docs exactly, yet encode Plus sendTx at 8,000 per minute, a Plus read pool of 120,000 weighted requests and Premium sendTx of 4,000–40,000 depending on staked LIT. Lighter's mainnet docs list Plus at 4000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute and 24000 weighted read-only requests per minute, and Premium up to 72000 sendTx/sendTxBatch per minute. Read the live docs instead of copying numbers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

In October 2025 a bot error pushed HYPE to $98 on Lighter, at a steep premium compared to global prices. Lighter said a runaway bot jammed through the HYPE book with size, that low volume was traded at very high prices, that there were no liquidations or other adverse effects, and that the wick was scrubbed from the front end. Crypto analyst Duo Nine, quoted by CoinDesk, said removing the data masks deeper liquidity issues. Lighter's docs make price on a taker order the worst acceptable price: if the sequencer cannot offer an equal or better price, the order is cancelled. (high confidence)

Premium/Advanced sendTx/sendTxBatch capacity scales with staked LIT: 4000 per minute at 0 LIT, 5000 at 1000, 12000 at 100000, 24000 at 300000 and 72000 at 500000. Lighter documents 72,000 transactions per minute as the Premium/Advanced maximum on Lighter mainnet (24,000 on Robinhood Chain). Fee credits count as staked LIT for this purpose. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts are gated by a volume quota that is enforced only for those tiers. Only L2CreateOrder, L2CancelAllOrders, L2ModifyOrder and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume quota; single-order cancels do not. Quota is earned per fill at 1 quota per $1 or $2 of notional depending on the market, shared across sub-accounts of one L1 address, and every 15 seconds the account gets one free sendTx. A sendTxBatch of n transactions consumes n quota. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Per-account order caps differ by tier. Standard allows 50 pending (TP/SL/TWAP) and 250 active orders per account, with 10 pending and 30 active per market. Premium/Advanced allows 1000 pending and 1500 active per account, with 100 pending and 1000 active per market. Transaction-type limits apply to all tiers, for example 40 requests/minute by default and for L2UpdateLeverage, and 2 requests/minute plus 3 per 2 hours for L2Withdraw. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

API trading goes through the sendTx and sendTxBatch REST endpoints or the jsonapi/sendtx and jsonapi/sendtxbatch WebSocket types. Every transaction is signed with SignerClient, which uses a signer binary whose code is in the public lighter-go repo. Each order carries a nonce, integer prices and sizes, and a client order index unique across all markets. HTTP code=200 only means the syntax was accepted; the sequencer can still reject the order. (high confidence)

On 16 Nov 2026 one transfer of 10,393,057 USDC at 10:11 UTC (about 10.39 million USDC) left Lighter's Ethereum contract to a single wallet, which Bitquery traced through CoW Swap to ETH and on toward Hyperliquid. Lighter said its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure and official SDKs were not compromised. Lighter paused withdrawals and pool creation and switched on Guardian mode; Guardian mode was later disabled, withdrawals resumed, and its Security Council returned approximately $5 million in USDC to the affected trader. (high confidence)

Per Lighter's postmortem as reported by Crypto Briefing, the affected accounts used signing code outside the official SDKs that repeatedly reused cryptographic nonces, so private keys could be reconstructed from publicly available signatures. The attacker used the keys to create a public pool from the affected account, acquired pool shares through a separate account, transferred the victim's funds into the pool and redeemed the shares. (medium confidence)

After the incident Lighter requires wallet signatures for transfers into public pools and made API key signatures nonpublic. It plans to introduce IP allowlists, configurable API key permissions and automated monitoring for nonce reuse, and advised traders using custom or third party signing software to rotate their API keys and switch to its official SDKs. Lighter's documentation says API keys can place trades, manage positions and move funds between accounts tied to the same wallet, as reported by Cointelegraph via MLQ. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

Transaction-type limits apply beyond the tier buckets: a default of 40 requests per minute, L2Withdraw 2 per minute and 3 per 2 hours, L2UpdateLeverage 40 per minute, L2ChangePubKey 300 per minute and L2Transfer 120 per minute. NautilusTrader reports that amending on every quote drift hit Lighter Mainnet `code=23000` (`Too Many Requests`) after roughly 40 modifications in a minute, and advises setting `sendtx_quota_per_min` to 40 or lower for transaction-heavy quoting. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts, not Standard, are gated by a volume quota. Only L2CreateOrder, L2CancelAllOrders, L2ModifyOrder and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume it (a batch of n transactions consumes n; single-order cancels are free). New accounts start at 1,000 quota and switching up from Standard resets it to 1,000. Most markets earn 1 quota per $1 of fill notional, but BTC, ETH and SOL stay at the $2 default of 1 quota per $2. Quota is shared across sub-accounts, a free transaction is granted every 15 seconds, trading alone refills it up to 15,000,000, and Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts can buy it through POST /api/v1/buyVolumeQuota at $500 per 1M quota. No-fill quote refreshes can exhaust it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter's /changeAccountTier endpoint switches account tiers. Upgrades can happen at any time, and downgrades require a 24-hour cooldown after the last tier change and a sub-account count that fits the lower tier. Since an August 2026 announcement, changing account type no longer requires closing positions or orders. The endpoint weighs 3000, which allows a maximum of 8 requests per rolling minute, and switching from Standard to Plus or Premium/Advanced resets the volume quota for the L1 address to 1,000. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Per-account order caps on Lighter mainnet scale with tier. Standard allows 250 active orders (30 per market) and 50 pending TP/SL/TWAP orders (10 per market). Plus allows 750 active (250 per market) and 500 pending (100 per market). Premium/Advanced allows 1500 active (1000 per market) and 1000 pending (100 per market). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

If the API accepted a transaction with code 200 but the outcome is unknown (timeout, dropped connection, no WebSocket confirmation), do not re-sign blindly. Check the transaction status by hash or the account_tx channel and compare nextNonce with the nonce you used. Re-signing with a new nonce while the original may still execute can place the order twice, and reusing the same clientOrderIndex rejects a second order only while the first is still open. NautilusTrader retains pending state on ambiguous delivery for reconciliation and does not resend the batch, and lighter-python issue 193 (open, with no comments) asks for an authoritative crash-safe recovery procedure and the meaning of the numeric status values. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Lighter's postmortem guidance for programmatic traders: sign with an official Lighter SDK (Python, Go, TypeScript or the Agent Kit), which generate every nonce with a cryptographically secure random number generator. With your own or third-party signing code, never derive a nonce from a timestamp, a counter, a weakly seeded random number generator, the transaction's contents or a cached value. Store keys securely and never share them or commit them to code repositories. If you are unsure whether your code has ever reused a nonce, rotate all of your API keys and switch to an official SDK. GoPlus adds that fixing the code alone isn't enough (revoke and replace all related API keys) and recommends enabling IP allowlisting and per-key permissions and limits as they become available. Lighter's API-keys docs separately say to use a read-only token, not an API key, for a dashboard, tax tool or AI agent. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Do not confuse the two nonces. The nonce in the Lighter incident is a one-off random value used by each signature: if the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. The transaction nonce in the SDK docs is tracked per API key, and failed transactions are re-signed starting from the current nextNonce. GoPlus states that signing nonces are distinct from transaction nonces. (medium confidence)

Per Lighter's August 2026 announcement, public pools can be created after reaching $10M in traded volume via a Plus or Premium account, without any sort of whitelist required. The November 16 attack used a public pool created from the affected account, and Lighter temporarily suspended all withdrawals and pool creation in a post at 11:02 UTC. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-30)

After the November 16 incident, Lighter's smart contract Guardian temporarily paused withdrawals and allowed ~5MM USDC to be returned to the affected trader by the Lighter Security Council; Guardian mode was then disabled, and Lighter announced that deposits and withdrawals were back to normal. Lighter now requires a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool. Sig and L1Sig inside info now return empty strings in transaction responses (tx, txFromL1TxHash, txs, accountTxs, blockTxs, block, blocks and account WebSocket channels), so identify transactions by hash and check their state using status. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16)

Scheduled downtime stops order placement. Lighter announced a network upgrade on Sunday, November 15 at 13:00 UTC with expected downtime under 20 minutes, told traders to manage positions in advance, and flagged another scheduled downtime on Sunday, November 22. It tells users they can programmatically monitor maintenances using Better Stack (status page for Lighter Core, robinhoodstatus.lighter.xyz for Lighter on Robinhood Chain), and publishes updates in the Telegram channel t.me/lighter_api_updates, labelled the official Lighter API updates channel. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

A report relayed by Phemex says arb.sh founder 0xTria revealed that a Relay solver stalled during frozen withdrawals and then repeatedly executed backlogged payments upon resuming at 19:14 UTC, generating 395 duplicate transfers within 25 minutes, totaling approximately $527,000 across 10 accounts. About $345,000 has been returned so far, leaving roughly $183,000 unrecovered. Neither Relay nor Lighter has issued an official response as of publication. (low confidence)

Lighter's own post-mortem, which a Cryptonews article says was published at 18:20 UTC on November 16, 2026, says an attacker gained control of a trader's API keys on the morning of November 16 (UTC) and withdrew funds. Lighter says its protocol, smart contracts and infrastructure were not affected. It says the keys leaked through the affected accounts' own signatures: the accounts used unsafe signing code other than the official Lighter SDKs, and that code reused signing nonces, which made the private keys recoverable from public data. Lighter says its official SDKs (Python, Go, TypeScript or the Agent Kit) generate every nonce with a cryptographically secure random number generator and were not affected. (high confidence)

Per Lighter, an API key can send funds to its own account's sub-accounts, and a public pool the account creates counts as one. The attacker used the leaked key to create a public pool from the affected account, mint pool shares in a separate, attacker-controlled account, transfer the affected account's funds into the pool (increasing NAV without minting pool shares), then redeem the shares and withdraw. Lighter says the attacker needed no access to the accounts or to Lighter's systems. (high confidence)

Lighter says it has already required a wallet signature to transfer funds to a public pool and made API key signatures non-public. It says it is still adding IP whitelists for API keys, permissions and limits configurable per API key (which actions a key may take and which markets it can trade), and monitoring signatures for nonce reuse, contacting affected accounts directly and proactively voiding affected API keys. A republished news report said IP allowlists and configurable permissions for individual keys remain planned. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

A Cryptonews analysis of Lighter's disclosure says Lighter does not publish the time Guardian triggered, so the length of the withdrawal freeze is unknown outside the company; it does not state the total value taken, only the amount returned; and it does not say whether the returned USDC came from funds recovered from the attacker or from the Security Council's own resources. The analysis also says nothing in the post establishes a general compensation policy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-18)

Lighter uses the word nonce for two different things. In the developer docs it is a per-API-key transaction counter (default new_nonce = previous_nonce + 1). In the post-mortem it is a one-off random value used by each signature, which must be unique and unpredictable; if the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. Lighter says never to derive a signature nonce from a timestamp, a counter, a weakly seeded random number generator, the transaction's contents or a cached value, and to use a cryptographically secure random number generator for every signature. (high confidence)

Volume quota rules for Plus and Premium/Advanced accounts: new accounts start at 1,000 quota, quota does not expire, and switching from Standard to Plus or Premium/Advanced resets the L1 address to 1,000. L2CreateOrder, L2ModifyOrder, L2CancelAllOrders and L2CreateGroupedOrders consume quota; a sendTxBatch of n transactions consumes n, grouped orders consume only one, and single-order cancels consume none. Every 15 seconds the account gets one free sendTx. The authenticated accountLimits endpoint's response schema includes volume_quota_remaining, volume_quota_cap and volume_quota_purchase_cap, together with user_tier_name, current_maker_fee_tick, current_taker_fee_tick and effective_lit_stakes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

lighter-python's repository page lists v1.1.9 as the latest release, dated Nov 18, 2026, among 25 releases, and requires Python 3.8+. Its nonce manager (pull request 162, opened Jul 6, 2026) fetches nonces lazily on first use per api key and holds a per-api-key asyncio.Lock across nonce assignment and send, so concurrent orders on one key arrive in nonce order while different keys send in parallel. Explicit nonce/api_key_index callers bypass the nonce manager entirely. For the current binary options discovery methods and response models, Lighter's troubleshooting page says to use lighter-sdk 1.1.8 or newer, or lighter-go v1.0.12 or newer. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Castle Labs measured Lighter's cost on public order books for crypto perps at $100,000. For BTC it reported slippage of 0.41 bps on Lighter, 0.21 bps on Hyperliquid and 0.07 bps for the centralised median (Binance, Bybit and OKX); adding the standard taker fee, the cost to open was 0.41 bps on Lighter, 4.71 bps on Hyperliquid and 5.07 bps for the centralised median. The data source was venue public APIs and order books on 23 September 2026, read at the same instant every 45 to 60 seconds for 10 to 20 minutes per session. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

On a Bankless episode (uploaded 2026-06-09), Delphi’s Flip and DeFi investor Will Price made the case for Lighter. A guest said taker or market orders wait on the order of 140 to 300 milliseconds depending on staking tier, that market makers don't know those orders are pending but can update where they quote as fast as their connection to the API permits, and that market makers can avoid getting picked off by toxic traders. (low confidence)

Reports on Nov. 17 say Lighter saw duplicate crediting after the withdrawal freeze. A KuCoin flash summary says that, according to 0xTria of arb.sh, a Relay solver that had been inactive during Lighter's withdrawal freeze replayed paused payment requests upon resuming, resulting in 395 duplicate transactions within 25 minutes, with 10 accounts receiving a total of $527,000. As of the report, $345,000 has been recovered, with $183,000 still unaccounted for, and neither Relay Protocol nor Lighter had issued a comment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

narrative.text: Lighter is a ZK-rollup perp and spot DEX on Ethereum with a central limit order book. Standard accounts pay 0% maker and taker on regular perp and spot orders; the cost is a 300 ms delay on taker orders, cancels and modifies, and a 60 requests/minute API limit. Plus (0.005%, higher rate limits) and Premium/Advanced (0.004% maker, 0.028% taker, 140 ms, LIT-staking discounts, up to 72,000 sendTx/min) are opt-in via the changeAccountTier endpoint. Trading uses SignerClient-signed sendTx over REST or WebSocket with per-order nonces. Operational risk is real: the Oct 2025 single-sequencer outage, and the 16 Nov 2026 theft of about 10.39M USDC through keys recovered from nonce-reusing custom signing code. Critics call the zero fee a latency tax.

Standard-account latency figures differ. The mainnet docs and the 2026-08-30 announcement give 300 ms taker, 300 ms cancel/modify and 0 ms post-only. A Medium review (Aug 2026) and the Robinhood Chain docs give 300 ms taker and 200 ms maker/cancel, and MarsBit and leviathan_news say 200-300 ms.

Scope of the 40 requests per minute default transaction-type limit. The rate-limits table lists it as the Default for all account types, while the Premium/Plus sendTx buckets reach 4,000 to 72,000 per minute. NautilusTrader observed code 23000 after about 40 modifications in a minute, which suggests it can bind order transactions, but the account tier of that test is not stated.

Cause of the incident. Lighter's first update called it a leaked API key on one trader's account and pointed at one compromised outside party (per Bitquery). Its post-mortem is more specific: custom signing code reused signature nonces, so the keys were recoverable from public signatures.
Whether the announced IP allowlists, per-key permissions and nonce-reuse monitoring have shipped.
Measured (not modeled) fill-quality difference between Standard and Premium accounts.

Does the 40 requests per minute default transaction-type limit cap order creation and modification on Standard, Plus and Premium accounts? The docs table and NautilusTrader's observation do not settle it.
Whether the ~5M USDC returned to the trader came from recovered attacker funds or Security Council resources, and when Guardian mode triggered. Lighter has not said.
